excerpt: Say that p is quasi-subsumed by q (in symbols: p ≲ q) iff there is some r such that p ∧ r ≤ q. Replacing ⊑∨ with ≤ in our original account of grounding, and ⊑∧∨ with ≲, delivers the following subsumption-theoretic analogue: (18) p1, p2, … < q iff: (i) p1 Ù p 2 Ù … ≤ q; and (ii) neither q ≲ p1, nor q ≲ p2, nor …
overview: The subsumption definition refines the earlier disjunctive-parthood analysis by connecting grounding to the idea that the grounds constitute a wholly relevant way for the grounded fact to obtain. It also supplies a route for comparing the authors’ account with nearby proposals in the grounding literature.
title: Subsumption Analogue
